name: Rates of reaction, collision theory and catalysts

terms.definition: Quantity of reactant used or product formed ÷ time taken.
terms.examiner: Units such as g/s or cm³/s; higher tier mol/s.

terms.definition: Reactions happen only when particles collide with enough energy (at least the activation energy).
terms.examiner: Rate depends on the frequency of successful collisions.

terms.definition: More particles in the same volume, so more frequent collisions.
A larger surface area exposes more particles, so collisions are more frequent.
terms.examiner: Smaller pieces or powder react faster.

terms.definition: Particles move faster, so they collide more often, and more collisions have energy greater than the activation energy.
terms.examiner: Both reasons are needed for full marks.

terms.definition: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up, by providing a different pathway with a lower activation energy.
terms.examiner: Enzymes are biological catalysts. Catalysts do not appear in the equation.

terms.definition: A straight line drawn touching a curve at one point; its gradient gives the rate at that time.
